subject: Multilingual A/B gating — acceptance criteria & product asks
messages:
From: Natalia Gomez <natalia.gomez@acme.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Multilingual A/B pilot — acceptance checklist request

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to pilot Redwood's multilingual prompt A/B feature for our customer support routing use case (Spanish + French). Before we kick off, can you send the acceptance checklist you use for multilingual A/B pilots? Specifics we care about: per-language quality thresholds, latency SLOs for short prompts (~20–80 tokens), and what falls under the "quality regression" gate vs. the "operational fallback" gate.

Also, would appreciate any recommended sample prompt distributions (token counts, common edge-case patterns) so we can share realistic test sets.

Suggest a 30‑minute sync today or tomorrow if that's easier.

Thanks,
Natalia
Product Manager, Acme AI

(External to Redwood)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Natalia Gomez <natalia.gomez@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-20T10:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Multilingual A/B pilot — acceptance checklist request

Hi Natalia — thanks for the clear ask. Copying the core Eval/Platform owners so we can align on a concise acceptance plan.

High-level proposal (quick bullets):
- Per-language acceptance is required: separate metric buckets for ES/FR.
- Primary quality metric: top-1 accuracy / intent match on labeled set + human-in-the-loop spot checks. Target: >= 92% per-language for control->variant acceptance.
- Safety/regression gate: any semantic hallucination rate increase > 2.5 percentage points triggers immediate rollback and investigation.
- Latency SLOs (short prompts ~20–80 tokens): p50 < 300ms, p95 < 900ms (measured from request arrival to first token emitted).
- Operational fallback: if latency SLOs are breached for 3 consecutive 10‑minute windows or error rate > 1.5%, swap to fallback model variant and alert oncall.

Attachments: I've attached a small template you can populate with sample prompt distributions and language splits (multilingual-a_b-template.xlsx). Also linking a working Drive doc below for collaborative edits.

Can we get Acme's sample prompt distribution by EOD tomorrow? If so, we can run a synthetic eval and come back with predicted pass/fail and any model/quantization recommendations.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Multilang-A-B

Thanks — I'll coordinate owners and a short checklist in the next message.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Natalia Gomez <natalia.gomez@acme.ai>
Date: 2029-07-20T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Multilingual A/B pilot — acceptance checklist request

Looping in product/ops specifics from my side. A few product asks we should lock before the pilot: 

- Gating policy: require a 5% canary for each language cohort (region-aware if traffic differs). If the variant passes both quality and latency thresholds at 5% over 48 hours, escalate to 20%, then full rollout.
- Model variant specification: define exact model name + quantization profile to avoid drift between runs. We should pin both control and variant config in the rollout plan.
- Metric alignment: ensure we record per-request model_id, quant_profile, and geo for debugging.
- Canary rollback conditions (quick):
  * Quality delta (control->variant) worse by > 2 pp on labeled set OR
  * Latency p95 increased by > 25% OR
  * Error rate spike to > 1.5%

I've created a Jira ticket for the rollout automation and canary checks: SUP-5123. Suggest we also include a short checklist file for CS/Eng (attached: canary-checklist.md).

Karthik
Sr PM, Product Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-07-20T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Multilingual A/B pilot — acceptance checklist request

Thanks — pulled together a lightweight acceptance matrix and sample eval plan. Key points:

- Suggested eval sizes: 1,000 labeled prompts per language for initial pass; stratify by intent and length (short/medium/long).
- Automated metrics: top-1 accuracy, BLEU (for templated responses), and a semantic similarity score (embedding cosine) for fuzzy matching.
- Human review: random 200-sample manual check per language; disagreements escalate to the senior evaluator.
- Regression alerting: wire the eval harness to both Slack #prod-evals and PagerDuty for regression-threshold breaches.

Attached acceptance-matrix.csv in case it helps. I'm available for a sync at 14:00 PT to walk through the matrix and finalize owners.
